newsitem.title: USA: Indiana United and P.T.C. set merger plan.
newsitem.headline: Indiana United and P.T.C. set merger plan.

text.p: Indiana United Bancorp Inc said Monday it agreed in principle to merge with P.T.C Bancorp, a one-bank holding company based in Brookville, Indiana, with assets of nearly $300 million.
According to terms of the proposed transaction, P.T.C. Bancorp shareholders will received 1.075 shares of Indiana United stock in exchange for each share of P.T.C.
Shares of Indiana United rose 1-1/4 to 40 on Monday.
The transaction is considered a merger of equals. The surviving company will retain the Indiana United Bancorp name and have combined assets of almost $650 million.
The proposed merger is expected to add to earnings of the combined company soon after the transaction is completed, officials from both companies said in a joint statement.

Robert Hoptry, chairman, president and chief executive of Indiana United will serve as chairman and chief executive of the combined company. James Saner Sr, president and chief executive of P.T.C. Bancorp, will serve as president and chief operating officer. The consolidated board of directors will be comprised of an equal number of directors from each comapny.
Upon completion of the merger, Indiana United will operate 28 offices in 12 counties in the southern and eastern regions of Indiana.

The proposed transaction requires a definitive agreement, and approval by regulators and shareholders of both companies. It is expected to be a tax-free reorganization that will be accounted for as a pooling of interests, they said.
The companies expect the transaction will be completed by the end of 1997.
